coarse.purpose: Bounded placement/prior ablation and separate manual-release diagnostics; no training acceptance

protocol.static_screen: Converged; BOTH selected tip residuals <=2mm, hand/self and object overlap <=2mm; no tower
protocol.selection: First four screened rows at distinct positions in fixed current/grid-x/grid-z/finger/weight order, frozen before physics

limitations: One-start soft IK and a coarse grid do not establish the full shared workspace or global impossibility.
Manual insertion is not simulated; empty reach and release are distinct episodes.
An initialized object can overlap soft collision surfaces by up to the diagnostic threshold; this is not proof of human placeability.
A stable loaded pinch is not force closure, a rotation skill or a validated training reset asset.

protocol.selection: Exactly frozen workspace candidates; no new optimization or selection

interpretation: Same two frozen Linux IK plans on both runtimes; no selection by physical outcome.
Native resets share four seeds but corrected physics naturally produces different initial object states.
Linux corrected candidate0 exceeds penetration and displacement limits; candidate1 rests with loaded thumb/middle but final normal dot -0.4714 fails the original -0.5 opposition threshold.
Mac corrected candidate1 passes this diagnostic, final normal dot -0.6344; cross-platform contact divergence precludes a robust grasp claim.
Manual insertion was not simulated. Object is initialized once in a separate release episode, preserving the physically reached hand.
All earlier v7 results remain historical legacy-physics results. Current formal 7/100, zero drops, quality_gate_failed remains unchanged.
Before further RL: register corrected task/checkpoint/controller semantics; verify grasp formation and hold with perturbations; then learn regrasp and rotation with new development/formal seeds.
